subtopics.title: Perfect Markets: Equilibrium, Profit and the Shutdown Point

questions.question: The individual perfect competitor's demand curve, told in words, is:
options: A horizontal line at the market price — demand, price, average revenue and marginal revenue all at once
A downward-sloping curve with marginal revenue below it
A kinked curve at the current price

questions.question: In the long run every perfect competitor earns only normal profit because:
options: Profits attract entrants whose supply pushes price down, and losses drive exits that lift it, until price touches lowest average cost

questions.question: A loss-making business should shut down in the short run when:
options: Price falls below average TOTAL cost
Price falls below the minimum of average VARIABLE cost, so each unit deepens the loss

questions.question: Under the Competition Act of 1998, the body that INVESTIGATES anti-competitive conduct is:

subtopics.title: Imperfect Markets: Monopoly, Oligopoly and Monopolistic Competition

questions.question: The monopolist's marginal revenue lies below its demand curve because:
options: Selling one more unit means lowering the price on every unit sold
Barriers to entry raise marginal cost

questions.question: The defining characteristic of oligopoly is:
options: Interdependence — each firm's best move depends on rivals' replies

questions.question: On the kinked demand curve, prices are sticky because:
options: A lone price rise loses customers while a price cut is matched at once — revenue falls in both directions

questions.question: Overt collusion, as against tacit collusion, means:
options: Following the leader's price without any agreement
A formal agreement such as a cartel — illegal under the Competition Act

subtopics.title: Market Failures, State Intervention and Cost-Benefit Analysis

questions.question: With a negative externality such as a tannery polluting a river, the market delivers:
options: Too much output at too low a price, because supply counts only private cost
Too little output at too high a price

questions.question: Street lighting is a public good because it is:
options: Non-rivalrous and non-excludable — free riding collapses private supply

questions.question: A maximum price set BELOW equilibrium produces:
options: A shortage — quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, with queues and black markets in its shadow

questions.question: Cost-benefit analysis tells the state to proceed with a project when:
options: The project creates any jobs at all
Social benefits exceed social costs, with unpriced consequences counted and future values discounted

subtopics.title: Contemporary Issues: Inflation, Tourism and Environmental Sustainability

questions.question: The inflation rate is calculated as:
options: New index minus old, divided by the OLD index, times one hundred
New index divided by new index
Old index minus new, divided by the new index
The repo rate minus the target band

questions.question: Wage settlements above productivity, a weaker rand and fuel increases are engines of:
options: Cost-push inflation — costs entering from the supply side

questions.question: Tourism absorbs job-seekers quickly because it is:
options: Labour-intensive and open at entry level

questions.question: Marketable pollution permits fight environmental damage by:
options: Capping total discharge and letting the right to pollute be traded, so cutting pollution earns money

subtopics.title: The Spaza and the Giant: Market Structures Made Plain

questions.question: The fruit sellers outside the station, all selling identical bananas at the given price, picture:
options: Near-perfect competition — price takers with flat demand lines

questions.question: The water utility is the street's giant because:
options: One network of pipes serves everyone and nobody digs a second — a monopoly a regulator must watch

questions.question: The spaza shops — each with its own late hours, good bread or trusted regulars — picture:
options: Monopolistic competition — many sellers, easy entry, differentiated corners

subtopics.title: When the Market Drops the Ball

questions.question: The taxi-washing bay pouring soapy runoff into the stream is a picture of:
options: A negative externality — a cost dumped on others that the wash price never counts

questions.question: Left alone, the street buys too little of the community study centre's service because:
options: Families weigh only their own benefit while the gains leak to every neighbour — a positive externality

questions.question: A minimum wage set above the going rate creates:
options: A surplus in the labour market — better pay for those who keep jobs, no job for some who never get hired

questions.question: Before building the new taxi rank, cost-benefit analysis tells the municipality to:
options: Count everybody's costs and benefits — displaced hawkers, saved commuting hours, air and noise — not only the items with price tags

subtopics.title: Prices, Tourists and the Planet in One Sweep

questions.question: Month-end crowds and easy credit letting shops mark up is the street's picture of:
options: Demand-pull inflation — prices pulled from the till side

questions.question: The one-sentence evaluation of the repo rate as an inflation cure is:
options: It fixes every kind of inflation equally
It cools flush spenders but cannot make diesel cheaper — strong on demand-pull, blunt on cost-push

questions.question: Tourism is called the export that never leaves home because:
options: Foreign visitors buy South African goods and services on South African soil — selling to the world without shipping

questions.question: The free dump keeps growing because:
options: Free things get overused — until the polluter is made to pay through levies, charges, permits and fines
